question: Why did studies finding moderate drinkers healthier than non-drinkers mislead people about alcohol as heart medicine?
answer: Because many of the non-drinkers had stopped because they were ill. Counting these sick quitters among abstainers made not drinking look risky. A 2016 review of 87 studies found that once such biases were corrected, the apparent life-extending benefit of moderate drinking largely vanished. The comparison group was sicker before anyone poured a glass.
move: Check who is in the comparison group before believing the comparison.
ask: When I compare myself with others, am I sure the group I am measured against is a fair one?
source: Stockwell et al., J Stud Alcohol Drugs, 2016
reference: Stockwell et al., Do moderate drinkers have reduced mortality risk? A systematic review and meta-analysis of alcohol consumption and all-cause mortality, Journal of Studies on Alcohol and Drugs, 2016
